name: Student protest at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, Kolkata
places: Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, Kolkata
about: Students at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute have protested since 27 September, when violence broke out on campus after protests greeted an event by a group affiliated to the RSS. They want accountability for the violence, the vice-chancellor Santosh Ajmera to resign, and rustication orders against six students withdrawn. Classes are suspended until 11 December.
demands: Accountability for the 27 September campus violence; resignation of vice-chancellor Santosh Ajmera; withdrawal of rustication orders against six students.

context.question: Why are students at Kolkata's film institute protesting?
context.short: Students at SRFTI in Kolkata have protested since violence on campus on 27 September. They want the vice-chancellor to resign; the institute has suspended classes until 11 December.
explainer: On 27 September protests greeted an event at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) organised by a group affiliated to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, and violence followed on campus. Students want accountability for it and say they were attacked inside their residential campus (Scroll).

On 15 October six students were served rustication notices over the alleged manhandling of the vice-chancellor (The Hindu). Students want those orders withdrawn and vice-chancellor Santosh Ajmera to resign. They marked a month of the agitation with a march across campus on 27 October.

In a statement on 27 October Ajmera said the protest had been 'turned into a platform for political and ideological battles, with demands that went beyond the institution's jurisdiction'. The institute says faculty and administration are ready to resume classes but a section of students keeps disrupting it. Class suspension has been extended to 11 December.
impact: Classes are suspended until 11 December, affecting academic life (The Hindu).
Police presence on campus is disputed: the administration put it at four or five personnel since 27 October, some students at around 50 (Scroll).
